questions.statement: ________ seen such a large and peaceful protest for human rights.
questions.context: Emphasizing a rare experience in activism.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Normal word order, no inversion.
Correct! When "Never" starts the sentence, the subject and auxiliary verb are inverted.

questions.explanation:
Cuando una oración comienza con un adverbio negativo o restrictivo como *Never*, el orden del sujeto y el verbo auxiliar se invierte, similar a una pregunta.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ protect children, but it also ensures their right to education.
questions.context: Emphasizing multiple benefits of a law.
questions.explanation:
La estructura *Not only + inversion... but also...* se utiliza para dar énfasis a dos hechos relacionados, resaltando que el segundo es tan importante como el primero.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ that the new policy would change their lives so drastically.
questions.context: Describing a situation where people were unaware of something.

options.feedback: Correct! Inversion after "Little" when used as a negative adverb.

questions.explanation:
Usamos *Little did they know* como una expresión enfática para indicar que alguien no tenía ni idea de lo que iba a suceder. Requiere el auxiliar *did* para la inversión.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ find a leader who is so committed to social justice.

options.feedback: Correct! Inversion after the frequency adverb "Rarely".
Incorrect. (Normal order, not inverted for emphasis).

questions.explanation:
Adverbios negativos como *Rarely*, *Seldom* o *Hardly* provocan una inversión cuando se colocan al principio de la oración para dar un tono más formal y enfático.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ had the speech ended ________ the audience erupted into applause.

options.feedback: Correct! "No sooner... than" is a fixed structure for inversion.

questions.explanation:
La estructura *No sooner + inversion + than* se usa para decir que una cosa ocurrió inmediatamente después de otra, con un tono muy literario o formal.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Only when people are educated ________ understand their fundamental rights.
questions.context: Setting a strong condition with "Only when".

options.feedback: Correct! When "Only when/if" starts the sentence, the second clause is inverted.
Incorrect. (Possible for general fact, but "will" is better for result).

questions.explanation:
Cuando empezamos una oración con *Only when*, la inversión no ocurre en la primera parte, sino en la cláusula principal que le sigue (*will they*).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is the most **emphatic** way to say: "I have seldom seen such bravery"?

options.text: I have seldom seen such bravery.
Seldom I have seen such bravery.
Seldom have I seen such bravery.
options.feedback: Correct! Uses inversion correctly for emphasis.

options.text: Never have I saw such bravery.

questions.explanation:
El estudiante debe reconocer que mover el adverbio al inicio y aplicar la inversión es la técnica gramatical estándar en el nivel B2 para elevar el tono y el énfasis.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "________ should we allow discrimination in our community."
questions.context: Understanding the restriction in "Under no circumstances".

options.feedback: Correct! A strong negative expression that requires inversion.

questions.explanation:
*Under no circumstances* es una frase hecha muy fuerte que se usa para dar órdenes o establecer principios innegociables. Siempre requiere inversión (*should we*).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ reached the podium when the protesters started to chant.
questions.explanation:
*Hardly had [subject] [participle] when...* es una estructura formal para describir dos eventos pasados que ocurrieron en una sucesión muy rápida.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Identify the error in this paragraph:
"Friends, **never before have we** (A) faced such a challenge. **Not only we must** (B) protect our families, but we also must fight for justice. **Only if we stand** (C) together **will we succeed** (D)."
questions.context: Identifying an error in a human rights speech.

options.feedback: Correct! After "Not only" at the start, we need inversion: "Not only must we".
Incorrect. Correct inversion in the second clause.

questions.explanation:
Un error frecuente es olvidar la inversión después de *Not only* al inicio de una frase. Debe comportarse como una pregunta: *must we*.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which slogan would be most effective for a formal human rights declaration?
questions.context: Choosing the most formal and powerful slogan.

options.text: We will never forget the victims.
In no way we will forget the victims.
Never shall we forget the victims of injustice.
options.feedback: Correct! High formal style with inversion using "shall" for a solemn promise.

options.text: Not only we remember them, but also we honor them.

questions.explanation:
En el lenguaje solemne de las declaraciones y discursos oficiales, la inversión (*Never shall we*) crea un impacto emocional y una autoridad que el orden normal no posee.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Choose the best completion:
"The struggle for rights is difficult. ________ have the activists been so organized, and ________ the importance of unity."

options.text: Seldom have / only now do they realize
options.feedback: Correct! Proper use of multiple inversions for a sophisticated argument.

options.text: Never have / only now they realized

questions.explanation: Este ejercicio final evalúa la capacidad de mantener el estilo enfático a lo largo de un párrafo, aplicando la inversión de manera consistente y variada.
